rows.evidence: A preserves all seven required fixes, four optional actions, and review context while making the findings easier to compare in one compact table. B is equally complete but repeats the same material through long bullet and inline sections, adding more scanning and cognitive load.

Both retain the registry boundary and marked source-derived fallback. B states the defect, consequence, and request as two direct paragraphs; A's bold restatement and courtesy wrapper add structure but make the comment feel more templated.
Both preserve commit-SHA pinning and the no-network offline replay boundary. B is shorter and reads naturally without losing the two-run identity consequence; A's title largely repeats its body.

Both request the shared parser and the offline defaults test. B keeps the failure mode and both actions in two compact sentences; A's heading and two-item action block are highly scannable but unnecessarily formal for this short comment.

Both retain finite-value validation, metric-specific rules, pre-result timing, and row-level routing to SourceConversionResult. B combines the two related actions naturally without weakening either; A's separate action scaffold adds bulk.

Both preserve the new-snapshot and legacy-snapshot actions. A conveys the defect, offline consequence, and two cases in two concise paragraphs, while B repeats the issue as a heading and adds a heavier action scaffold.

Both retain live-mode querying and unchanged offline behavior. B explains the present-null state as an entry already marked missing and gives the consequence plainly; A's phrase 'A known gap cannot discover' is awkward and briefly obscures the subject.

Both preserve exact-ID precedence and the single-owner condition for normalized names. B is a more natural, compact reviewer comment; A's bold title and 'Please make' phrasing add ceremony without adding information.

Both retain all four required concerns, the optional limit cleanup, boundaries, and requested tests. B's tables separate issue from action and make severity/location comparison immediate; A repeats findings across needs-attention bullets and inline comments and has a much denser run-details block.

Both preserve preflight, recoverable-old-file retention, route-transition completion, and multi-route failure tests. A is direct and uses the clearer phrase 'newly created files'; B's bullets scan well, but 'files that call creates' is awkward and the template is heavier than needed.

Both preserve the unstable identity input, raw dataset path replacement, and unchanged reconciled metadata/routing boundary. A is more direct and avoids the repetitive title-plus-body pattern; B's added parenthetical precision is useful but denser.

Both preserve exclusions-only accounting, stale-report replacement, atomicity, publication ordering, and clean-run coverage. A uses the established failure-report terminology and 'last complete report'; B's title and 'ledger' wording are less plain.

A retains both merge-readiness actions, all four optional suggestions, and their important conditions in compact tables with a direct opening. B is complete but spreads the same information through long bullets, duplicated inline comments, and an extensive uncollapsed details block.

Both preserve PR #221 as the prerequisite and require the post-rebase default-rich CLI check. A explains the hidden-warning path and action in two cohesive paragraphs; B fragments the same point into a title and four short blocks.

Both retain the mandated guide path and all three documentation points: alias trigger, warning-only result, and single-record evidence limit. A is shorter and reads like a natural review request; B's heading and courtesy wrapper add repetition.
